pages.quiz:
COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.

2. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

3. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.

4. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

5. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Remove all guards
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

6. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Speaker
   C. Keyboard
   D. Monitor

7. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.

8. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.

9. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

10. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. International Cricket Team

11. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Overload every socket
   D. Ignore burnt cables

12. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Network Standards and Protocols and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Network Security and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Implementation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.

2. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

3. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

4. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

5. D — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

6. A — CPU

7. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.

8. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.

9. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

10. C — Information and Communication Technology

11. B — Never touch live wires with wet hands

12. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Computer Network Standards and Protocols; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Object Oriented Programming Implementation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
